questions: What is the definition of "unique elements" - does it mean distinct values or distinct indices?
Can the same element be used twice if it appears multiple times in the list?
What should be returned for an empty list or a list with only one element?
Are duplicate pairs considered - for example, if both 5 and -5 appear multiple times, does that count as one valid pair or multiple?
What is the expected behavior when the list contains zero - can zero be paired with itself?
Should the function handle overflow cases where two large integers might sum to zero due to integer overflow?
What is the maximum size of the input list that needs to be supported?
Are there any constraints on the range of integer values that can appear in the list?
answers: 'Unique' (better: 'distinct') refers to distinct POSITIONS/indices in the list, not distinct values -- so two occurrences of the same value at different indices count as 'distinct elements' for pairing.
Yes -- the same value appearing at two different indices can be used as the pair (e.g. [0, 0] sums to zero using two distinct positions of the same value).
